3D forecast chart

Interactive 3D chart built for HydroTwin. X: forecast target date · Y: estimated gauge height (ft) · Z: the selected environmental reading on the earlier issue date. Orange is the forecast, blue is the observed-flow estimate; each line joins forecasts from successive issue dates at the same lead. Both height curves come from this station’s stage–discharge fit — they are estimates, not measured water levels, depth, or absolute elevation. Environmental readings show associations, not causation; soil and snow sensors can be far from the gauge.

Multi-factor correlation

How strongly each factor moves together with the others at this station — Pearson correlation on daily data, 2001–2026. Values run from −1 (move oppositely) through 0 (no linear link) to +1 (move together). The bottom row shows each factor against next-day log flow. Correlation is not causation: two factors can move together because a third drives both, or because both follow the seasons.

Station clusters

Fourteen stations, grouped by how their rivers behave, not by geography. Each station is described by its flow regime over the full daily record (2001 to 2026): average flow, flashiness, low flow share, peak month, seasonal swing, plus snowpack from the NRCS gauges, plus basin traits from the USGS NLDI: watershed area, the length of river below the gauge, and the flow each square kilometre of basin yields. A k means clustering on those traits (k = 6, chosen by silhouette score) finds six regimes. The first chart shows the groups themselves in trait space, the first two principal components of the same traits, so stations that plot close together genuinely behave alike; the map shows where each regime lives; a Ward hierarchical clustering draws the family tree below.
